clue.text: Bill gets into modified grader for a test of acceleration

indicators.note: something modified has been changed, so the following word's letters are rearranged
one thing getting into another ends up placed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: An invoice slipped inside a tinkered road grader, as though testing how fast the machine can go.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is the usual crossword abbreviation for account, hence bill; it sits between DRAGR and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a short sprint between cars from a standing start, purely a contest of speed off the line.

clue.text: Artful type of lead-swinger?

blocks.note: first meaning: the Artful one, the pickpocket nickname in Oliver Twist
second meaning: one who swings the lead, a shirker who avoids work

explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the young pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist; to swing the lead is British slang for shirking work, which is what a dodger does.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens nickname names a crafty character, and the plain noun means a person who avoids duty or work.

clue.text: Passages could be first-rate with less activity

indicators.note: activity suggests movement, so the word before it is stirred into a new order

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Corridors might be ideal if fewer people bustled through them.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a standard way of saying first-rate, and the 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aisles are walkways between rows of seats or shelves, so they are passages in a church, theatre or shop.

clue.text: It's on the right in beam - something very unusual

indicators.note: sitting on the right side of something means being written just after it
in says the combined piece sits inside the word for beam

blocks.note: a ray is a beam of light
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that something sits to the right of a beam, then a verdict that it is a strange sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The right' does double duty: it supplies the abbreviation and says the pronoun goes to its right, after it, before the pair goes inside the beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is a thing seldom found or seen, an uncommon item or occurrence.

clue.text: Chanel wants fruit reserved - a fair thing?

blocks.note: Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer
a nut is botanically a kind of fruit
a reserved person is shy

explanation.surface: A fashion designer asks for some fruit to be set aside for her.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls to knock coconuts off posts.
explanation.definitionFit: This stall is a traditional attraction at funfairs, so it is something found at a fair.

clue.text: Promenade rots away needing pounds to complete

indicators.note: rots away pictures the word crumbling apart, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the symbol for a pound, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A seaside promenade decays and needs money spent to finish it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pounds as a plural gives two Ls, as pence can give PP.
explanation.definitionFit: To promenade is to walk at leisure, especially in public, which is what a stroll is.

clue.text: Let it stand up around the skating area's cheap ornamentation

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom
around means the turned word wraps the next piece

blocks.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand
a rink is a skating area; the 's adds the S

explanation.surface: Leave the cheap baubles decorating the ice rink just where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of skating area's is the link 'is', so it adds no letter; TETS wraps RINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinkets are small ornaments or jewellery of little value, so cheap decoration.

clue.text: Overtake tourist cruising around before parking

indicators.note: cruising around suggests wandering in no fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A sightseer drives about before finding somewhere to leave the car, passing other vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip someone is to go faster than and get ahead of them, the same as passing them.

clue.text: Independent action by one who may have just one suit?

definitions.text: one who may have just one suit?

blocks.note: first meaning: acting alone, without help

blocks.clueFragment: one who may have just one suit?
blocks.note: second meaning: a solitary worker, or in card games a player who goes it alone

explanation.walkthrough: The suit looks like clothing; in whist-style card games a player who plays a hand alone holding strength in one suit is said to play a lone hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means doing something entirely on your own, and is also a card-game term for playing without a partner.

clue.text: I'd return to particular area

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
particular and strict both mean exacting

explanation.surface: Someone says they would go back to one specific place.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a region or neighbourhood marked off for some purpose, an area of a town or country.

clue.text: Models look around for a kind of glove

indicators.note: around says the second word is wrapped about the first

blocks.note: mien is a person's look or bearing
the Ford Model T gives T, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Fashion models glance about while choosing gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Ford's famous early car, so models can be two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten is a glove with one section for all four fingers and another for the thumb.

clue.text: Choosing to give politician a job?

blocks.note: first meaning: picking one option
second meaning: voting someone into office hands a politician employment

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that giving a politician a job is a playful picture of voting.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to choose, and especially to choose by vote someone for public office.

clue.text: Small two-masted sailing boat seen in outline

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a ketch is a sailing vessel with two masts

explanation.surface: A little yacht spotted as a silhouette on the horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or brief plan giving only the main features, which is an outline.

clue.text: Hale and almost hearty, upset about key fitness programme

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the following word is dropped
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
about means the jumbled letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its final letter removed
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A robust person, nearly in the pink, gets annoyed about the regime meant to keep them fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Health care is the organised provision of medical and preventive services to keep people well.

clue.text: This shows us the way outside

definitions.text: This shows us the way outside

blocks.clueFragment: This shows us the way outside
blocks.note: surface reading: something pointing out the exit of a building
setter's reading: a direction marker standing out of doors by the road

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like an exit sign indoors; the thing meant stands outdoors giving the name or route of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A post or plate on a road naming it or pointing towards places directs people while they are out in town.

clue.text: All but fifty getting ready for battle - it's shocking!

indicators.note: all but means everything except, so the letter for fifty is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, the letter removed
arming is preparing for war

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone readying for war is a disturbing sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one L from ALL leaves AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming causes fear or dismay, so it is shocking.

clue.text: It's held up by floundering novice being forced out

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word reads from the bottom
floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters lose their order
held by means gripped inside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A struggling beginner holds things up while being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Eviction is the legal removal of a tenant from a property, being made to leave.

clue.text: Access to transport

blocks.note: first meaning: a way in, stressed on the first syllable
second meaning: to delight or enrapture, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.walkthrough: Transport looks like vehicles, but here it means carrying someone away with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a door or way in, and the verb means to fill with wonder, as transport does in its rapturous sense.

clue.text: A wretched situation for those not late

blocks.note: plain sense: a state of misery
setter's reading: late means dead, so this is a torment for people still alive

explanation.walkthrough: Late, as in the late Mr Smith, means deceased; those not late are alive, and their hell is one on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an unbearably miserable experience suffered in this life rather than after death.

clue.text: Remove little dash of greasepaint and bury the hatchet

blocks.note: first meaning: the word for greasepaint is written with a hyphen, and dropping that little dash gives the two-word entry
second meaning: to be reconciled after a quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: The little dash is a hyphen, not a dab of paint: take it out of the cosmetic word and the phrasal verb remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical cosmetics are make-up, and to end a quarrel and become friends again is to make up.

clue.text: A country race

blocks.note: first meaning: a sovereign state
second meaning: a people sharing descent, language or culture

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a cross-country running event, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a state with its own government and a large group of people united by common descent.

clue.text: Protest march mounted within city limits - that should raise a laugh!

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means lifted so the word reads upward
limits are the edges, so only the outside letters are kept
within places the turned word inside the kept letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A demonstration is staged inside the city boundaries, and someone hopes it will be funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is entertainment designed to amuse, so it ought to make people laugh.

clue.text: Rocker arranged to stop again

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock musician is organised so as to halt once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To recork a bottle is to put the stopper back in, so to stopper it a second time.

clue.text: Fort supplying a hot meal

indicators.note: supplying suggests the following letters are the material from which the answer is made up

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A garrison provides its soldiers with a warm dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo is the mission fort in San Antonio, Texas, besieged in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous Texan mission was used as a fortress during the siege that made it a byword for a last stand.

clue.text: Bumps on the head got in pub around ten on Sunday

indicators.note: around means the word for pub is placed round the number
on means the next piece is attached at the end

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
ten written as the figures 1 and 0, read as letters
S is short for Sunday

explanation.surface: Someone collected bruises on the skull in a bar brawl around ten o'clock on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten as IO is a crossword convention. 'Got in' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The inion is the bony knob at the back of the skull, so inions are protrusions on heads.

clue.text: Enables one to proceed from starting point

blocks.note: surface reading: something that lets a person move forward
setter's reading: the reference level from which progress is measured

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a permit; it is the reference line from which change is measured.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseline is the initial level or standard against which later measurements are compared.

clue.text: Spice Girls' start in Germany

indicators.note: a start is a beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written
GER is the abbreviation for Germany

explanation.surface: The Spice Girls began their career in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger Spice was Geri Halliwell's nickname in the 1990s pop group the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is a pungent root used as a kitchen seasoning, and also the name of one of the band members.

clue.text: Any power could have this armament

indicators.note: could have suggests a possible version, so the letters may be reordered into another form

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Every nation might own this military hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry is weapons collectively, the arms and equipment of a fighting force.
